definition: Debase means to lower the quality or esteem of something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word debase. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know debase should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Selling knighthoods to anyone with the fee debased an honor that soldiers had bled for.
Cheapen is far milder than debase — a tacky ad can cheapen a brand for a season without changing what the product is; to debase it is to lower the real worth underneath.
Ruin goes further than debase — a debased honor still gets awarded, just respected less; a ruined one no one will accept at all.

Devalue is the ledger's word: it lowers what something is worth in money or measurable terms — a currency, a stock, a house. Debase cuts deeper than any price tag, draining the esteem a thing commands, so a debased honor can cost nothing and still have lost everything.

To water down a thing is to weaken it by dilution — a watered-down rule or drink still exists, only thinner and fainter. Debase passes a harsher judgment: the thing is not merely weaker but lowered, worth less in quality and in everyone's esteem.

When Coach Reyes started at Lincoln, the team's Iron Wolf jacket was earned, not given: four years of showing up early, and the roster voted on every name.
The boosters changed that.
Jackets went to top fundraisers, then to their siblings, then to anyone photographed at three home games.
Nothing about the jacket itself changed — same wool, same stitched wolf — but seniors began leaving theirs in lockers.
'They debased it,' the coach said flatly.
'The price of the wool held.
What it stood for didn't.' This fall, two players asked whether they could earn the old kind instead.
